questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $1.9M in MI's 8th District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is offense.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
DCCC (a party committee) has spent $266K in NV's 3rd District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Does a 501(c)(4) nonprofit that runs election ads have to disclose its donors?
questions.why: It must report the ad spending, but generally not its donors unless they gave for that ad. That's why it's called dark money.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $569K in OH's 15th District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is defense.

questions.prompt: Can a corporation give unlimited money to a super PAC?
questions.why: Since Citizens United and SpeechNow.org (2010), corporations, unions and individuals can give super PACs unlimited sums.

questions.prompt: SLF PAC (a super PAC) has spent $8.2M in the AK Senate race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Can a corporation give directly to a candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Corporations and unions can't contribute to federal candidates. They can form PACs, or give to super PACs.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
In CO's 5th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $1.8M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $966K.
